question: Is the supplied terminal production-hook proof plus focused regression coverage enough to land this compaction `sessions_send` replay filter, or should maintainers require a live two-agent timing proof first?
rationale: The patch is narrow and source-backed, but it changes a session-state/message-delivery recovery boundary where green CI cannot fully prove the intermittent live timing shape.

options.title: Accept Scoped Proof
options.body: Proceed after exact-head checks because the proof exercises the production compaction hook and the regression tests cover replay removal plus safe-text preservation.

options.title: Require Live Timing Proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a redacted two-agent compaction recovery run shows one delivered reply and preserved safe source context.

options.title: Pause For Broader Boundary Review
options.body: Pause this PR only if maintainers want replay safety handled by a broader transcript, delivery, or API contract instead of a local fallback filter.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Proof
recommendation.body: Proceed after exact-head checks because the proof exercises the production compaction hook and the regression tests cover replay removal plus safe-text preservation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current history on the central compaction safeguard and agent runtime boundary that this proof decision affects.
